duplicate-logic-rule.desc: Verifies that no run of statements is repeated anywhere in the codebase. Every duplicated run is reported as a group: the set of locations that share it.
duplicate-logic-rule.equivalence: Two runs are duplicates when one can be turned into the other by renaming identifiers (i.e. a "p-match", or Type-2 clone), and/or by substituting a small number of leaves.

holes.desc: A "hole" is one spot where the copies in a group have the same shape but disagree on a leaf: a field name, a method name, a literal, or a type. The hole count is the number of such spots, which is the number of parameters the shared helper would have to take. Copies differing in anything but leaves (an operator, an extra statement) are not a group at all.
holes.example: `x.health <= n` and `x.attack <= n` are one group with one hole: the field. The helper takes one accessor parameter.
holes.note: A hole at a field or method name costs a closure or accessor parameter, not a plain value, so it is a more expensive extraction than a literal hole. The violation report names the kind of each hole.

duplicate-logic-rule.config: - min_stmts: how short a repeated run may be before it is a violation; runs of fewer statements than this are ignored (default 2). - max_holes: how many holes a group may have and still be a violation; 0 means the copies must match exactly after renaming (default 4). - min_nodes_per_hole: how much shared structure each hole must have as a count of syntax nodes; groups below this are too small to be worth a parameter and are ignored (default 16). - ignore: list of group ids to skip (copy them from the violation report)
